Rashi on Chullin 88a:10:1.english: Chaff - Areste [Old French for chaff/shives] that they shake out from the flax:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:1:1.english: And these and those do not impart ritual impurity - because the Rabbis did not decree ritual impurity upon them:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:1:2.hebrew: ואלו ואלו תחלה - שאפילו שני מטמא משקין להיות תחלה, כדתנן (לעיל חולין דף לד.): "כל הפוסל את התרומה" — דהיינו שני — מטמא משקין ועושה אותן תחלה, חוץ מן הטבול יום:
Rashi on Chullin 88a:1:2.english: And both these and those are first-degree [ritually impure] - For even [a source of] second-degree [impurity] renders liquids impure to become first-degree [impure], as we learned in a Mishnah (above, Chullin 34a): "Anything that disqualifies terumah" — which is second-degree [impurity] — renders liquids impure and makes them first-degree [impure], except for a tevul yom [one who immersed himself that day].

Rashi on Chullin 88a:1:3.hebrew: תחלה - ראשון לטמא שני, והשני שלישי:
Rashi on Chullin 88a:1:3.english: First [degree] - First [degree], to render [something] second [degree], and the second [renders something] third [degree]:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:1:4.hebrew: חוץ ממשקה שהוא אב הטומאה - כגון שלשה מעיינות הזב המנויין במס' נדה בפרק דם הנדה (נדה דף נד:), שהן אב הטומאה לטמא אדם וכלים: זובו, ורוקו, ומימי רגליו, ושכבת זרעו של כל אדם, דילפינן מרוק, דכתיב (ויקרא ט״ו:ח׳) "וכי ירוק הזב" — מה רוק שהוא מתעגל ומתאסף יחד ואחר כך יוצא, אף כל שהוא מתעגל ויוצא. ומשקין אחרים יוצאין ממנו שאינם אב הטומאה, לפי שאינם מתעגלים ויוצאין כרוק, ואלו הן: דמעת עינו, דם מגפתו, וחלב האשה:
Rashi on Chullin 88a:1:4.english: Except for a liquid that is a primary source of [ritual] impurity - For example, the three secretions of a zav enumerated in Tractate Niddah, in the chapter [entitled] Dam HaNiddah (Niddah 54b), which are a primary source of impurity to render people and vessels impure: his discharge (zov), his spittle, and his urine, as well as the semen of any man — which we derive from spittle, as it is written (Leviticus 15:8): "And if the zav spits" — just as spittle forms a globule and collects together and then issues forth, so too anything that forms a globule and issues forth [is a primary source of impurity]. And other liquids issue from him that are not a primary source of impurity, because they do not form a globule and issue forth like spittle, and these are they: the tear of his eye, the blood of his wound, and a woman's milk:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:2:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: "מאי לאו קלין שרץ וזב וחמורין מת" - מת חמור הוא, שהוא אבי אבות הטומאה:
Rashi on Chullin 88a:2:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: "What, is it not [that] minor [sources are] a creeping animal and a zav, and major [sources are] a corpse" - A corpse is [considered] major because it is an avi avot hatumah [the highest level of ritual impurity]:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:2:2.english: A creeping animal - such as the urine of a creeping animal that is found in its bladder:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:2:3.hebrew: לא קלין שרץ וחמורין זב - אבל משקה המת טהורים, חוץ מדמו שהוא מטמא מן התורה, כדכתיב (במדבר ו) "על נפש מת":
Rashi on Chullin 88a:2:3.english: No, minor [sources refers to] a creeping animal and major [sources refers to] a zav - However, the liquids of a corpse are ritually pure, except for its blood, which imparts ritual impurity by Torah law, as it is written (Numbers 6): "near a dead body [nefesh]" [i.e., its blood]:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:3:1.hebrew: מאי שנא זב דגזור רבנן - מיהא טומאה מתחלה במשקין שאינן אב הטומאה כגון מעיינות, ומאי שנא מת דלא גזור:
Rashi on Chullin 88a:3:1.english: What is different [about] a zav, that the Rabbis decreed - at any rate, first-degree ritual impurity in liquids that are not a primary source of impurity [like] bodily secretions [ma'ayanot], and what is different [about] a corpse, that they did not decree:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:3:2.hebrew: זב - לפי שהוא חי, לא בדילי אינשי מיניה, ועוד שאינו ניכר לכל:
Rashi on Chullin 88a:3:2.english: A zav - Because he is alive, people do not separate from him, and furthermore, [his condition] is not noticeable to everyone:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:4:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda said, etc. - Further on, [the Gemara] explains his reason:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:5:1.hebrew: אגפיים - כותלי בית השחיטה. ולשון אגפיים כמו אגפי המים, גדותיה:
Rashi on Chullin 88a:5:1.english: Agapayim [sides] - [This refers to] the walls of the place of slaughter. And the term "agapayim" is like "agpei hamayim" [the edges of the water], [meaning] its banks:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:5:2.hebrew: אבל כסה דם הנפש כו' - ושלש מחלוקות הן: רבנן סברי כוליה בעי כסוי; ולרבי יהודה, אפילו דם הנפש לא בעי כסוי אלא מקצתו, כדקתני דדם הניתז פטור מלכסות ואפילו הוא דם הנפש, ובלבד שיהא שם דם אחר; ולרבן שמעון בן גמליאל, דם הנפש כוליה בעי כסוי:
Rashi on Chullin 88a:5:2.english: But if he covered the blood of the soul, etc. - And there are three opinions [in this dispute]: the Rabbis hold [that] all of it requires covering; according to Rabbi Yehudah, even the blood of the soul does not require covering, except [for] part of it, as it teaches that spurting blood is exempt from covering even when it is the blood of the soul, provided that there is other blood there; and according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, all of the blood of the soul requires covering:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:6:1.english: The Rabbis hold [that] "its blood" [means] all of its blood - [it] implies [this]:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:7:2.english: A lid - [that] which is on the mouth of a barrel:

Rashi on Chullin 88a:9:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו דצריך ולא צריך - ללישנא קמא, דאמר "אין צריך" קרי חול הדק ומותר — האי נמי בכלל "אין צריך" הוא, ותורת חול הדק עליו, ומותר; וללישנא בתרא, דקרי חול הגס ואסור כל שצריך לכותשו — האי נמי בכלל "צריך לכותשו" הוא, וחול הגס שמו, ואסור:
Rashi on Chullin 88a:9:1.english: There is [a difference] between them [with regard to sand] that requires [crushing] and does not require [crushing] - According to the first version, which says [that whatever] does not require [crushing] is called fine sand and is permitted — this [crumbling sand] is also included in [the category of] "does not require [crushing]," and the legal status of fine sand applies to it, and it is permitted; and according to the latter version, which calls "coarse sand" — and forbids — anything that requires crushing — this [crumbling sand] is also included in [the category of] "requires crushing," and its designation is "coarse sand," and it is forbidden:

Tosafot on Chullin 88a:6:1.hebrew: רבנן סברי דמו כל דמו - ואע"ג דאמרינן בפרק זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כה.) דאימתי דרבי יהודה לפרש, היינו דוקא במשנה, אבל בברייתא לא; דבכל הספרים גרסינן בסוף חלון (עירובין פא:): כל מקום שאמר רבי יהודה במשנתינו "אימתי" וכו'. ואומר ר"ת דהכא הלכה כרבי יהודה, דמתניתין כוותיה אתיא; דאע"ג דבברייתא על כרחך בא לחלוק, במתניתין אתא לפרש. ומיהו לרמי בר חמא (ורב חסדא) משמע בזה בורר (סנהדרין דף כה.) דאף במשנה הוי "אימתי" לחלוק היכא דמוכח, והכא מוכח כיון דבברייתא בהדיא פליגי רבנן. ולרבי ירמיה בפ"ק דגיטין (דף ז: ושם ד"ה אומר) הוי לחלוק אע"ג דלא מוכח, גבי ספינה, דמשני: הא רבי יהודה והא רבנן, והיא משנה במסכת חלה (פ"ב מ"ב). וי"ס דגרסי בברייתא קמייתא: "וכסהו, מלמד שדם הניתז ושעל אגפיים חייב לכסות; אמר רבי יהודה כו'", תניא אידך: "וכסהו, מלמד שכל דמו חייב לכסות; מכאן אמרו כו', רשב"ג אומר כו'". ולפי גירסא זו יכול להיות דברייתא באה לפרש, והא דקאמר "ורבנן סברי", אדרבנן דרשב"ג קאי:
Tosafot on Chullin 88a:6:1.english: The Rabbis hold [that] “its blood” [means] all of its blood - Even though we say in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 25a) that Rabbi Yehuda’s [expression] “When [is this said]?” comes to explain [and not to disagree], that is specifically in a Mishnah, but not in a baraita; for in all the texts we read at the end of [the chapter entitled] Chalon (Eruvin 81b): “Wherever Rabbi Yehuda says in our Mishnah ‘When [is this said]?’ etc.” And Rabbeinu Tam says that here the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda, since our Mishnah accords with him; for even though in the baraita he perforce comes to disagree [with the Rabbis], in our Mishnah he came to explain. However, according to Rami bar Chama (and Rav Chisda), it is implied in [the chapter] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 25a) that even in a Mishnah “When [is this said]?” comes to disagree where it is evident [that he is disagreeing] — and here it is evident, since in the baraita the Rabbis explicitly disagree [with him]. And according to Rabbi Yirmiyah in the first chapter of Gittin (7b, and there s.v. Omer), it comes to disagree even where it is not evident, regarding [the case of] a boat, where [the Gemara] answers: “This [reflects] Rabbi Yehuda, and this [reflects] the Rabbis,” even though it is a Mishnah in tractate Challah (2:2). And there are texts that read in the first baraita: “‘And he shall cover it’ — this teaches that blood that spurts out and [blood] that is on the sides [of the neck] one is obligated to cover; Rabbi Yehuda said, etc.” [And] it was taught in another [baraita]: “‘And he shall cover it’ — this teaches that one is obligated to cover all of its blood; from here they said, etc.; Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says, etc.” And according to this reading, it is possible that the [first] baraita comes to explain, and that which [the Gemara] says “and the Rabbis hold” refers to the Rabbis [who dispute] Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:

Tosafot on Chullin 88a:6:2.hebrew: ורבי יהודה סבר דמו ואפילו מקצת דמו - תימה, דבפ"ק דבכורות (דף ג.) סברתם הפוכה: דרבנן סברי "בכור" — אפילו מקצת בכור, כתיב "כל" עד דאיכא כוליה; ורבי יהודה סבר "בכור" — כוליה בכור, כתיב "כל" דאפילו כל דהו. ואומר ר"ת דהכא הוי כמו התם: דמשום ד"דם" כוליה דם משמע, קא"ר יהודה "דמו" — מקצת דמו, דוי"ו ד"דמו" אתא לאפוקי ממשמעותיה ד"דם", כדאמרינן התם: כתב "כל" דאפילו כל דהו. וקשה לפירושו, דהא לעיל קאמר רבי יהודה "דמו" לחלק. ועוד, לפי מה שפוסק ר"ת הכא כרבי יהודה, קשה הלכתא אהלכתא, דאמרינן בבכורות (שם:): לית דחש להא דרבי יהודה דאמר שותפות עובד כוכבים חייב בבכורה. לכן נראה שאין לדמות הדרשות, אלא מה שהש"ס מדמה, כי ההיא ד"בתולה" מקצת בתולים, דמדמה בפרק אלמנה נזונית (כתובות צז:) לפלוגתא דמקצת כסף ככל כסף, דהוו ענין אחד: דכשנתמעטו בתוליה ונשארו מקצתן, כאילו נשארו כולן; וכן כסף אשה בכתובתה, כשנשאר מקצתה יש לה מזונות כאילו נשאר כולה. אבל "שה" מקצת שה דפליגי רבי אליעזר ורבנן, ופלוגתא דרבי יהודה בן בתירא ורבנן ב"כל נפש", ו"חמש" ולא חצי חמש, ו"חמשה בקר" ולא חמשה חצאי בקר — אין לדמותם יחד. ועוד יש לתרץ דלא תקשה דרבי יהודה אדרבי יהודה דבכורות: דהתם דווקא משמע ליה "בכור" כוליה בכור, דקרא מסתמא משתעי בסתם בהמות דכולה דישראל, בבהמת ישראל; א"נ, משום דכתיב "כל בכור בישראל", משמע כוליה דישראל, כדאמר בפרק מצות חליצה (יבמות דף קב.): "בישראל" — עד שיהא אביו ואמו מישראל:
Tosafot on Chullin 88a:6:2.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds "its blood" — even a small amount of its blood - This is astonishing, for in the first chapter of Bekhorot (3a), their reasoning is reversed: the Rabbis hold [that] "firstborn" (bekhor) [implies] even part of a firstborn, [so] "all" (kol) is written [to teach that it is not subject] until all of it [belongs to a Jew]; whereas Rabbi Yehuda holds [that] "firstborn" [implies] all of a firstborn, [so] "all" is written [to teach] that even any small amount [makes it subject]. And Rabbeinu Tam says that here it is like there: for because "blood" (dam) implies all of the blood, Rabbi Yehuda says "its blood" (damo) [means] part of its blood, as the vav of damo comes to exclude [it] from the plain implication of dam, just as we say there: [Scripture] wrote "all" [to teach] that even any small amount [is included]. However, this is difficult according to his explanation, for above Rabbi Yehuda said [that] "its blood" [is written] to separate [between obligations]. Furthermore, according to what Rabbeinu Tam rules here in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, one halakhic ruling contradicts another halakhic ruling, for we say in Bekhorot (ibid., 3b): No one is concerned for this [view] of Rabbi Yehuda, who says that a partnership with a non-Jew is obligated in the law of the firstborn. Therefore, it appears that one should not compare [different] Scriptural expositions except where the Talmud itself compares [them], like that [dispute] of "a virgin" [meaning] part of [her] virginity, which [the Talmud] compares in the chapter [entitled] Almanah Nizonet (Ketubot 97b) to the dispute of "part of the money is like all of the money," for they are one [and the same] concept: for when her virginity was diminished and part of it remained, it is as though all of it remained; and similarly [with] a woman's money in her ketubah, when part of it remains, she is entitled to sustenance as though all of it remained. However, [the dispute over] "a lamb" [meaning] part of a lamb, where Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis disagree, and the dispute of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira and the Rabbis regarding "any person," and "five" [shekels] and not half of five, and "five oxen" and not five half-oxen — one should not compare them together. And furthermore, one can answer so that [the view of] Rabbi Yehuda [here] does not contradict [the view of] Rabbi Yehuda in Bekhorot: for there specifically "firstborn" implies to him an entire firstborn, because the verse without further specification speaks of ordinary animals, which belong entirely to a Jew — [i.e.,] of an animal of a Jew. Alternatively, because it is written, "every firstborn in Israel," it implies [one that is] entirely of a Jew, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Mitzvat Ḥalitzah (Yevamot 102a): "In Israel" — [meaning] until his father and his mother are from Israel:

Tosafot on Chullin 88a:7:1.hebrew: חרסית - פי' בקונטרס במרובה (ב"ק דף סט.): לבנה כתושה. וא"א לומר כן, דהכא חשיב תרוייהו. וכאן פי' בקונטרס: חרסית — שחיקת חרסין. וגם על זה קשה, דברייתא בגמרא חשיב תרווייהו:
Tosafot on Chullin 88a:7:1.english: Charsit - Rashi explained in [the chapter entitled] Merubah (Bava Kamma 69a) [that it is] a crushed brick. However, it is impossible to say so, for here [the Mishnah] counts both of them. And here Rashi explained [that] charsit [is] ground potsherds. Yet this too is difficult, for a baraita in the Gemara counts both of them:

Tosafot on Chullin 88a:7:2.hebrew: כל דבר המגדל צמחים כו' - לאו לפלוגי אתא, אלא לעשות כלל לדבר. ואם תאמר: והא חרסית אין מגדל צמחים, כדמשמע במרובה (שם) דאמר "סימנא כי חרסית דליכא הנאה מינה"! ואומר ר"ת דלעולם מגדל, ו"ליכא הנאה מינה" דקאמר, היינו שאינו מוציאה כדי נפילה. ואין ראיה מן המדרש דקאמר "אם חרסית היא, פירותיה רזין", דהא קאמר נמי "ואם צונמא היא, פירותיה שמנים", וצונמא לאו בר זרעים היא, כדקאמרינן באלו עוברין (פסחים דף מז:); אלא כעין חרסית וכעין צונמא קאמר:
Tosafot on Chullin 88a:7:2.english: Anything in which plants grow, etc. - [Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel] did not come to disagree, rather to state a general rule for the matter. And if you will say: But charsit [crushed potsherd / clayey soil] does not grow plants, as is implied in [the chapter entitled] Merubah (there), where [the Gemara] says, "A mnemonic: like charsit, from which there is no benefit"! Rabbeinu Tam says that it certainly does grow [plants], and [what] it says, "there is no benefit from it," means that it does not yield [produce] equal to what was cast [into it as seed]. And there is no proof from the Midrash that says, "If it is charsit, its fruits are lean," for it also says, "And if it is tzunama [hard rock], its fruits are fat," whereas tzunama is not fit for seeds, as we say in [the chapter entitled] Eilu Overin (Pesachim 47b); rather, it means "like charsit" and "like tzunama":
